source.title: AI Daily Digest — 2026-11-05
source.body:
# AI Daily Digest — November 5, 2026

**Top story: OpenAI published the first end-to-end account of an AI system doing offensive security at industrial scale — and the price tag.** An autonomous pipeline built on an unreleased cyber model ran against the Linux kernel's master branch in mid-October, triaged **2,308 candidate findings**, dynamically reproduced **1,724 vulnerabilities**, and produced **948 working local privilege-escalation exploits** plus 948 candidate patches, for **$1,213,430** in API credits. The same 24 hours brought Anthropic's **FlashProve** work on cryptographic proofs of inference and OpenAI's cyber model **Daybreak Red** reaching AWS GovCloud. Running against all of it: American voters rejected data centers in **40 of 41 local ballot measures** on Tuesday, and Nikkei put the five biggest US tech firms' off-balance-sheet AI obligations at **~$3.2 trillion**, roughly double six months ago. The labs are shipping security capability faster than the public is granting them permission to build the buildings.

**A note on this edition's sourcing.** This session's network policy blocked direct access to **arXiv (including export.arxiv.org), Hugging Face, TechCrunch, The Verge, Hacker News, openai.com, worldlabs.ai, trending-repos.com, theneuron.ai and aiweekly.co**. **anthropic.com and raw.githubusercontent.com were reachable and were read directly**, and GitHub's repository-search API was reachable for named repositories (star and fork counts below are from it, read today). Everything else rests on web search results and the secondary coverage they surface; where a primary source could not be checked, the entry says so. The arXiv listing section in particular could not be verified against arXiv itself.

---

## Notable Papers & Research

### OpenAI: 948 Linux kernel root exploits, built and priced
**November 4.** OpenAI published *"A thousand fewer paths to root."* An automated pipeline — **Scout** agents selecting kernel code by reachability from low-privileged users and security relevance, then **Analyst** agents working the targets — ran against the kernel master branch in **mid-October 2026** and produced **948 distinct local privilege-escalation exploits**, each dynamically reproduced, along with **948 candidate patches**. Reported end-to-end cost: **$1,213,430** in API credits. OpenAI says it has sent hundreds of reports and patches for critical vulnerabilities to Linux maintainers, with the remainder going out through its *Patch the Planet* partners; one account puts **61 fixed upstream** at announcement time. Technical detail was withheld for safety.

**Why it matters:** this is the first time a frontier lab has published both the yield and the unit economics of autonomous vulnerability research at this scale, which makes the defensive arithmetic concrete — and makes the same arithmetic available to anyone who can rent the compute. **What to discount:** the patches are *candidates generated by the pipeline*, not 948 fixes shipped to the kernel. Circulating "bounty value" figures of **$18.9M–$66.3M** are extrapolations from Pwn2Own/TyphoonPWN comparisons, not awards, and a separate ~$1.5M figure refers to a different hardened-kernel test of 21 vulnerabilities — the two should not be combined. Sources also disagree on unique vulnerabilities versus exploit count. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/a-thousand-fewer-paths-to-root/) · [unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/openai-pipeline-finds-948-linux-kernel-privilege-escalation-flaws/) · [Interesting Engineering](https://interestingengineering.com/ai-robotics/openai-agents-linux-kernel-vulnerabilities-exploits)

### Anthropic: FlashProve — zkSNARK proofs that a response came from the model you were promised
**Published November 2, updated November 3** (read directly on anthropic.com today; it reached the top of Hacker News on the 5th with 179 points). Authors: **Roy Rinberg** and **Alex Allain** (Anthropic); **Alessandro Chiesa** (EPFL, StarkWare); **Miranda Christ** (MIT, RESI); **Rahul Dalal** (Anthropic STEM Fellows Program, Succinct); **Giacomo Fenzi** (EPFL); **Ben Mayer** (Anthropic Fellows Program, MIT); **Guy Weissenberg** (EPFL). From the **Frontier Red Team**.

The problem it states plainly: a user querying a model today cannot verify the response came from the model the developer claims, rather than one swapped in by a routing service for cost reasons or by an attacker tampering with the token stream — and output quality alone is not evidence. The work advances **zkSNARKs** for provable inference, chosen for their hiding and efficiency properties, through a system called **FlashProve**. **Why it matters:** the post names **verifying compliance with AI pacing requirements** as an application, which puts a cryptographic primitive directly underneath the governance debate Amodei opened in September — pacing commitments you can check rather than take on trust. The post carries its own limitations section; treat it as progress, not a deployable guarantee. [Anthropic — provable inference](https://www.anthropic.com/research/provable-inference)

### Anthropic: the first 3D structure of a prokaryotic vault particle
**November 4** (read directly on anthropic.com). Anthropic's biology research lab reports the **first 3D structure of a vault particle found in prokaryotic cells**. Vaults are large hollow protein barrels — roughly three times the mass of a ribosome — discovered in 1986 by **Leonard Rome** and **Nancy Kedersha**, present in nearly all cells in the human body, and of **still-unknown function**. Claude was used at each step: searching across sequence literature, optimizing a particle-isolation method, and mapping the structure from cryo-EM data. A **preprint has been submitted to bioRxiv** and is not yet live.

**Why it matters:** this is the second such result in two weeks (after *"How Claude designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins,"* October 20), and the framing is a deliberate one — an AI lab publishing wet-lab structural biology under its own name, with the model as co-investigator rather than literature search. **What to hold back on:** no peer review yet, and the preprint link is still pending, so the structure itself is unreviewed. [Anthropic — vault particles](https://www.anthropic.com/research/investigating-vault-particles-with-claude)

### "Sparks of Weight-Space Programming" — an LLM editing another model's weights directly
**Posted November 3**, by **Rikiya Takehi** and co-authors (MIT-affiliated per secondary coverage). The claim: a general-purpose LLM can read a neural network's weights and write new values into them without gradients or a training loop. Across eight experiments with **GPT-6 Astra**, the reported headline result is diagnosing repetitive reasoning loops in **Qwen3.5-0.8B** and changing **0.016% of its weights** to lift **MATH-500 from 7.9% → 48.1%** and **GSM8K from 13.8% → 67.1%**. The authors also report Astra writing small game-playing policy networks from scratch, zero-shot.

**Why it matters:** if it generalizes, model repair becomes an inference-time edit rather than a training run — and Karpathy's "Software 2.0" framing of weights as code written by an optimizer acquires a second author. **Why to read it carefully:** the demonstrated cases are small networks and single, localized faults; a community note points out the weights were supplied as text in the prompt, with the model using code and forward passes, which weakens the word "natively." Not peer-reviewed. [Takehi's blog](https://rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming/) · [Takehi on X](https://x.com/rikiyatakehi/status/2117313742891327994) · [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/11/03/forget-retraining-ai-can-now-tweak-another-ais-weights/5307105)

### From the November 4–5 arXiv listings
**Caveat first, and it is a large one:** arXiv and its API were both unreachable this session. The items below come from third-party auto-generated digests of the cs.AI/cs.CL/cs.LG listings ([news-radar #979](https://github.com/datnguyenquy94/news-radar/issues/979) for 11-04, [agents-radar #4129](https://github.com/duanyytop/agents-radar/issues/4129) for 11-05), read via GitHub's search API. **Titles, IDs, author lists and every reported figure are unverified against the papers themselves** — the author attributions in particular come from a generated summary and should not be quoted. Treat these as leads.

- **[You don't need long context](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05306)** — reports that periodic compaction (summarising earlier tokens) cuts inference cost up to **7×** on frontier models while holding benchmark accuracy on long-input tasks. The most directly actionable claim in the batch if it holds.
- **[Suppressing Misaligned Behaviors in Language Models, Durably](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05358)** — builds deliberately misaligned "model organisms," then tests which suppression techniques survive further fine-tuning rather than letting the behaviour re-emerge.
- **[Aligning Language Models with General Preferences: Direct Nash Optimization](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05373)** — frames alignment as a two-player game approximated to a Nash equilibrium via on-policy sampling, positioned as an alternative to RLHF pipelines.
- **[Modality-Aware Expert Pruning for MoE-Based Multimodal LLMs](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05927)** — claims up to **90%** memory reduction in MoE multimodal models without performance loss.
- **[SlackBench](http://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05512)** — a benchmark putting agents on real code repositories alongside human collaborators, part of a visible shift this week toward evaluation on real rather than synthetic work (also **MedPhysBench**, **TandemBench**).

---

## Model & Product Launches

### Reserved slot: Tencent Hunyuan Hy4 — vision and computer use *(company not covered elsewhere in this digest)*
**November 4.** Tencent's Hunyuan team launched the official version of **Hy4**, successor to the **August 28** Hy4 preview. Chinese press reports it as a **~770B-parameter mixture-of-experts** model with a **1M-token context window**, and — the part that makes it notable — Tencent's **first model with vision and computer-operation capabilities**, able to drive both graphical interfaces and command lines. Priced at **6 yuan per million input tokens**, unchanged from the preview. Live across Tencent's own surfaces: **Tencent Cloud TokenHub, WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao, ima** and the WeCom assistant **Dayuan**, with third-party routing appearing on OpenRouter and others. A cheaper **Hy4 Flash** is promised "soon."

**Why it's the reserved item:** computer use from a Chinese lab at frontier scale, shipped into a consumer and enterprise install base of WeChat proportions, is a different kind of distribution event than an API launch. **What is not settled:** the **preview was open-sourced in August; whether the official release has public weights is contested** — some outlets call it open source, at least one says not yet. Tencent's benchmark claims (including a reported Terminal-Bench figure) are vendor-reported with no independent evaluation available, and several details come from low-profile aggregators. Check Tencent's own Hy4 page before relying on either the license or the numbers. [Caixin Global](https://www.caixinglobal.com/2026-11-05/tencent-launches-upgraded-hy4-ai-model-with-visual-understanding-102501068.html) · [Tencent Hunyuan — Hy4](https://hy.tencent.ai/research/hy4) · [PANews](https://panews.io/articles/01a1a509-67cb-767f-b692-bac8d93c7f9e)

### Kimi K3.1 Pro open weights have landed — the follow-up to yesterday's deadline
Yesterday's digest recorded November 4 as Moonshot's promised weights date with nothing shipped as of writing. **The weights are now public**, at `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro` on Hugging Face: **2.8T total parameters, ~104B active per token**, **MXFP4** weights with MXFP8 activations, **~1.56 TB across 96 safetensors shards**, **~1M context**. The API has been live since **October 23**.

**Why it matters:** this is now the largest set of openly downloadable frontier weights, and it gives self-hosted coding agents a route that does not pass through a US API. **Three things to check before acting on it.** The **date is disputed** — sources variously say November 2, 4 and 5. The **license is disputed and matters**: one account says the weights do *not* ship under a standard open-source license, another describes MIT-style use/modify/fine-tune rights, and a third reports a clause requiring hosted-service businesses above **$20M revenue** to sign a separate agreement; read the model card yourself. And the **benchmarks are Moonshot-reported** — claims range from "beats Opus 5.5 on 16 of 37 tests" to "within 0.7 points on Terminal-Bench 4.0" to a composite methodology putting the best open-weight model **12 points behind**. [Startup Fortune](https://startupfortune.com/moonshot-ai-releases-full-weights-for-28-trillion-parameter-kimi-k31-pro/) · [AlphaSignal](https://alphasignal.ai/news/moonshot-ai-opens-kimi-k3-1-pro-weights-to-beat-claude-on-coding-agents)

### OpenAI ships ChatGPT Images 2.6 — GIFs, reference images, two API models
**November 4.** *"Images, upgraded—introducing ChatGPT Images 2.6. Now with GIFs and reference images."* ([OpenAI on X](https://x.com/OpenAI/status/2118124944928432327)) Prompts or uploaded images become **animated GIFs** with adjustable speed and per-frame editing; users can save **reference images** of themselves, pets or characters for reuse across generations. Reported **50% faster** than Images 2.5 and more consistent across repeated edits, plus **image markup** and **SVG export**, and a **complexity parameter** controlling how much the model plans before rendering. Available on **every tier including free**, across web, desktop and mobile, in ChatGPT and Codex. Two API models shipped: **GPT-Image-2.6 Flare** (fast, as little as six seconds, lower quality) and **Sunburst** (quality and edit consistency) — though The Decoder notes both variant names were introduced with Images 2.5, so the API lineup is less new than it reads. OpenAI says users generate about **4 billion images per week**; a system card was published. [The Decoder](``https://the-decoder.com/chatgpt-can-now-turn-text-prompts-and-photos-into-animated-gifs-with-openais-images-2-6-model/``) · [System card](https://deploymentsafety.openai.com/chatgpt-images-2-6)

### Cognition SWE-2 Flash — 3× faster, one-fifth the price, weights withheld on cyber grounds
**November 4.** Cognition launched **SWE-2 Flash**: **276B total / 12B active parameters**, adapted from **Thinking Machines Lab's Inkling-Small** base model, in **Devin Desktop** and the **Devin CLI**, **free through November 30**. Pitched for routine work — automations, code review, feature development, documentation. **No standalone API pricing**, and **weights stay private**, with Cognition citing cybersecurity risk and describing a planned secure weight-sharing program for partners and researchers.

**The benchmarks are worth reading as published, because Cognition's own numbers are mixed:** Flash edges SWE-2 on FrontierCode 2.0 (**24.0% vs 23.8%**) but *loses* on SWE-Bench Pro v2 Hard (**89.9% vs 90.6%**), Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE 1.1. The claim to weigh is the price-performance one, not a frontier one — and a lab withholding weights on cyber-risk grounds on the same day OpenAI publishes 948 kernel exploits is not a coincidence of calendar. Self-reported; no independent verification found, and secondary sources give conflicting Terminal-Bench figures. [unite.ai](https://www.unite.ai/cognition-launches-swe-2-flash-for-faster-lower-cost-coding-agents/) · [explainX](```https://explainx.ai/blog/cognition-swe-2-flash-inkling-small-mid-training-276b-a12b-free-devin-claimed-vs-verified-2026```)

### Daybreak Red reaches AWS GovCloud
**OpenAI's page is dated November 4** (AWS's own announcement is dated October 30 — the dates conflict). **Daybreak Red**, OpenAI's cyber offering built on **GPT-5.6 Cyber**, is now available to eligible customers on **Amazon Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (US-East)** and US East (Ohio), for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation and security testing. Verified defenders get fewer refusals alongside stronger identity verification, monitoring and access controls. OpenAI says inference data is not used for training and customers need not share Daybreak Red data with OpenAI. **Access requires separate OpenAI approval *and* AWS provisioning** — one does not grant the other. No public pricing. Read alongside the 948-exploit post above: the capability and the government-cloud distribution channel for it arrived the same day. [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/daybreak-red-aws-govcloud/) · [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/10/openai-daybreak-red-govcloud-east/)

### Claude Mythos — Watchlist Update
**No new information today, and one piece of circulating coverage should be discounted.** The shipped state of the line remains **Mythos 5.1** (September 1, 2026), restricted to verified organizations, **$10/M input and $50/M output**, 1M context. The **"Claude Mythos 5.5"** string spotted in Anthropic's page source around November 1 and subsequently removed — reported here yesterday — has produced nothing further: **no announcement, no release date, no comment from Anthropic**. **Anthropic's news and research pages, read directly today, show the two research posts above (November 2 and November 4) and nothing about Mythos.**

**A caution on search results:** queries for Mythos news currently surface a BleepingComputer piece on Mythos "coming to Claude Code" with a `claude-mythos-1-preview` string spotted in a toggle. **That report is from around May 2026**, not this week, and it predates the entire 5.x line. It is not a new signal.

### World Labs (Fei-Fei Li) — Watchlist Update
**No new model, product or blog post, and no new statement from Li.** **Atlas** (September 1) remains early access with selected partners — still **no paper, model card, parameter count or training-compute disclosure**. **Marble**, the first commercial product, remains the shipped artifact.

**The live thread is still the AMD close, and it is still open.** AMD's **$8.2B all-stock** acquisition was announced **September 28** (agreement signed September 26), with **Li to join AMD as EVP and chief scientist reporting to Lisa Su**. AMD said it expects to **close by the end of 2026**, subject to regulatory approval. **Five and a half weeks on, no closing announcement has appeared.** Li's most recent on-the-record remark remains the deal press release: *"Joining AMD will give our team the resources and engineering depth to accelerate our research and help define the infrastructure needed for the next era of AI."* With roughly eight weeks left in AMD's own window, the absence of a closing notice is the thing to watch. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/28/amd-fei-fei-li-world-labs.html) · [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-and-ml/2026/09/28/amd-bets-82b-that-worlds-matter-more-than-words-in-ai/5299609)

---

## Key Opinions & Statements

### Altman spends a day defending a remark about your RAM
**Sam Altman** told **John Collison** on the *Cheeky Pint* podcast last week that it is *"quite terrible"* for everybody to keep a share of the world's limited DRAM in their own computer, *"used 5% of the time"* — arguing scarce memory produces more value in data centres, where it runs continuously. The backlash ran through **November 4**: gamers facing a memory shortage were loudest, some posts crossed into threats, and **Elon Musk** piled on — *"The people deserve to have their RAM too!"*

Altman's response, same day: he **changed his X display name to "RAM Altman,"** said the comments were taken out of context, called the episode *"f***ing annoying,"* said he has argued for years that the world should ramp up memory production, and posted *"I want you to have so much RAM."*

**Why it is worth more than a gossip line.** The context critics supply is specific: Altman signed letters of intent with **Samsung** and **SK Hynix** in October 2025 for Stargate memory, which one critical outlet estimates locks up around **40% of global DRAM production** — a figure to treat as that outlet's estimate, not a disclosure. DDR5 kit prices in Japan are reported up as much as **761%** year-on-year for some high-capacity configurations, and both Samsung and SK Hynix have said AI-driven shortages run **into 2027 and beyond**. The dispute is not over his words, which are quoted consistently; it is over whether the CEO of the largest single buyer of the scarce part gets to characterise consumer demand for it as waste. It is also the first time this cycle that AI infrastructure cost has landed on ordinary consumers as a *price they personally pay* — which, read next to Tuesday's data-center votes, is the same political story arriving by a different route. [Gizmodo](````https://gizmodo.com/sam-altman-youre-completely-right-about-ram-im-sorry-for-the-confusion-heres-what-happened-2000835208````) · [Video Games Chronicle](`````https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/fing-annoying-sam-altman-claims-comments-about-pc-gamers-buying-ram-taken-out-of-context/`````) · [Tom's Hardware](``````https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/elon-musk-mocks-openai-ceo-sam-altmans-claim-that-pcs-having-ram-is-terrible-the-people-deserve-to-have-their-ram-too)``````

### A correction worth making, because the misdating is circulating
Searches for Amodei's November statements currently surface a page carrying his line that *"for too long, the industry lied to people about the fact that this technology had risks,"* timestamped November 5. **The quote is real but it is from mid-September** — a **CBS Sunday Morning** interview the day after *"We Must Pace the Frontier"*, covered by Forbes on **September 13**. There is no new Amodei statement today. Do not repeat it as November commentary. [Forbes (Sept 13)](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2026/09/13/dario-amodei-says-ai-industry-lied-about-technologys-risks/)

### A quiet day for the rest of the tracked list
- **Andrej Karpathy** — nothing new. His last substantive post remains **HackerTube** (November 1): 43M Hacker News comments over 20 years filtered by Claude down to 6,454 recurring video recommendations, built in *"~2 hours with Opus 5.5."* Covered in an earlier edition.
- **Demis Hassabis** — nothing new. Most recent remains the **WSJ Magazine** interview (~October 22), where as WSJ's 2026 Technology Innovator he called recent incidents of models going rogue *"warning shots"* for the industry.
- **Yann LeCun** — nothing new. **AMI Labs** has still shipped no model since its **$1.03B** seed in March; LeCun remains executive chairman with **Alex LeBrun** as CEO.
- **Ilya Sutskever** — nothing new. **SSI** has published no model, paper or product since the July Nvidia partnership.
- **Dario Amodei** — nothing new today (see correction above).
- **Fei-Fei Li** — nothing new (see World Labs watchlist).

---

## Other Notable AI News

### Voters rejected data centers in 40 of 41 ballot measures
**Preliminary results from Tuesday, November 3.** Ballotpedia counted **41 local measures across 10 states** aimed at restricting data-center construction. Per CNBC, voters sided against data centers in **every one but Harwood, North Dakota** — where the measure that failed would have *added* extra review for industrial projects, so even the exception is not a pro-data-center result in the ordinary sense. **Ohio alone had 21.** In **Wells, Maine**, more than **80%** backed a retroactive **180-day moratorium**; early results in **Alhambra, California** showed over **80%** for a ban. There were **no statewide** data-center initiatives. Opposition crossed party lines — Capital B News notes a majority of Republicans oppose new construction in their own communities, matching a Politico poll cited by Forbes.

**Why it matters:** compute siting has become a retail electoral issue, decided locally, at a moment when the five largest buyers have committed trillions to building it (see below). Counts differ slightly between outlets ("nearly 40" vs 41), some measures were advisory rather than binding, and these are early results. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/data-center-ballot-measures-2026-midterm.html) · [Scientific American](https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/2026-election-results-show-widespread-opposition-to-ai-data-centers/) · [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/zacharyfolk/2026/11/04/heres-where-voters-are-rejecting-data-centers-at-the-ballot-full-list/)

### Nikkei: off-balance-sheet AI obligations at the big five now ~$3.2 trillion
**November 4.** Nikkei Asia's compilation puts the **off-balance-sheet AI-related obligations** of **Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Oracle** at roughly **$3.2 trillion** as of end-September — up about **90%** in six months from Nikkei's July figure of ~**$1.65 trillion**, which already exceeded the ~**$1.35 trillion** those firms carried *on* balance sheet. Roughly **60% purchase commitments, 40% future lease obligations** not yet begun. Nikkei puts **Meta** at about **$420 billion**, nearly triple its ~$58.7B reported long-term debt.

**Read it carefully.** This is a **compiled estimate of AI-related commitments, not a disclosed figure**, and Nikkei does not publish a precise methodology; a separate tally from Kalkine puts Meta at **$866 billion**, a gap that almost certainly reflects scope rather than one party being wrong. The direction of the funding mix is the signal, not the decimal. Enron comparisons are circulating; the structures are ordinary purchase and lease commitments, which is a different thing from fraud. [Nikkei Asia](https://asia.nikkei.com/business/technology/artificial-intelligence/us-tech-giants-hidden-ai-debt-swells-90-to-3.2tn-in-6-months) · [Telecompaper](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/us-tech-giants-ai-related-obligations-surge-to-usd-32-trn-report--1587755)

### Two developer-tools acquisitions in one day: Meta buys Conductor, OpenAI to buy Pierre
**November 4.** **Meta acquired Conductor**, whose software splits a project across several parallel AI coding agents — first reported by **Axios**, confirmed by the founders, terms undisclosed. CEO **Charlie Holtz** said he will work with Meta chief AI officer **Alexandr Wang** and **Nat Friedman**, who leads product at Superintelligence Labs; **Jackson de Campos** is the other co-founder. Conductor was founded in 2024 on a **$22M Series A** from Spark Capital and Matrix Partners. **The wind-down is fast and worth noting if you use it:** Conductor Cloud **shuts down November 20**, **write access ends November 13**, and the local Mac app loses support in early 2027.

The same day, **OpenAI announced it will acquire Pierre Computer Company**, maker of the Git-based **Code Storage** and the open-source **Diffs** and **Trees** tools, to fold into **Codex** — putting it more directly against GitHub. The deal is **pending customary regulatory approvals** and the companies operate separately until close; terms undisclosed; existing Code Storage customers keep access and the open-source projects stay open with continued OpenAI contribution. Pierre raised a **$22M Series A** in November 2025 from CRV and 01A, and its technology is already used inside Codex. *(Note: some HN commentary read "Pierre Computer" as a chip play. It is source control, not silicon.)* [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/04/meta-acquires-ai-coding-startup-conductor) · [OpenAI](https://openai.com/index/openai-to-acquire-pierre/) · [devops.com](https://devops.com/openai-acquires-pierre-computer-to-expand-codex-challenge-github)

### Anthropic paid a news publisher for the first time — AP election data, timed to the midterms
**Reported November 4 by Adweek**, sourced to two people familiar with the matter: **Anthropic signed a licensing deal with the Associated Press** just before the US midterms — its **first time paying a digital news publisher** for content. Claude served **real-time, attributed AP election data**; users asking for polling updates saw information *"provided by and attributed to the Associated Press."*

**Why it matters, and the limits.** Anthropic had resisted formal publisher partnerships while OpenAI accumulated more than a dozen, and its **$1.5B authors' class settlement** is a legal resolution, not a license. Adweek's own framing is cautious: this limited foray *"is by no means an indicator that Anthropic has irrevocably changed its licensing strategy."* **Neither company has disclosed financial terms, duration or scope**, neither has confirmed on the record, and whether this is a one-off election arrangement or a strategy shift is unknown. Note separately that Anthropic's **election-safeguards post** currently surfacing in searches is dated **October 14**, not this week. [Adweek](https://www.adweek.com/media/anthropic-licensing-deal-ap-election/) · [Mediagazer](https://mediagazer.com/261104/p17)

### Google: schools that ban AI lose Search — then the political backlash, then the clarification
**November 3–4.** The **New York Times** reported that Google's AI tools are **off by default for K-12 student accounts** until administrators enable them — but that schools restricting AI **altogether lose Google Search**, because AI features are now built into the engine. Districts including **New York City** and **Los Angeles** had already banned generative AI for many or all students this year. **Sen. Bernie Sanders** and **New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani** criticised the company; Google then said schools are in control and that **Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search can each be enabled individually** — Search without Gemini products. Google education VP **Chris Phillips** still told the Times that *"Search and AI are deeply integrated."* **The terms remain unclear:** at least one account describes the post-backlash arrangement as Search returning *with AI Overviews*, which is not the same as Search on its own. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/03/google-responds-to-outrage-over-removing-search-in-schools-that-ban-ai.html) · [TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/03/google-will-let-schools-disable-its-ai-tools-but-not-without-sacrificing-search/) · [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/google-shut-search-schools-opt-ai-rcna607280)

### Postman silently installed AI plugins into developers' coding agents
**Hacker News' biggest AI thread of the week** — **1,489 points, 484 comments** by November 5 — is [postmanlabs/postman-app-support#14370](https://github.com/postmanlabs/postman-app-support/issues/14370), alleging that **Postman desktop 12.33.4** silently installed AI plugins into **Codex** (plugin 1.1.0) and **Claude Code** (plugin 2.0.1). **[NVIDIA/auto-ontology](https://github.com/NVIDIA/auto-ontology)** — *an open library that builds a semantic context layer over enterprise metadata and serves it to any agent harness.* Apache-2.0, Python, **5,551 stars** (reported **+2,050 today**, the largest single-day gain on the board), 439 forks, 46 open issues. The README states the problem better than most: *"a revenue metric answered faster is worth nothing if the number is wrong."* Five verbs — **Discover** (generate ontologies from metadata, connect existing semantic models, build knowledge graphs), **Ground** (give agents trusted meaning for metrics and entities, reconcile inconsistent definitions across systems), **Validate** (check generated queries against certified definitions and lineage, return provenance with every answer), **Expose** (serve context via **MCP, CLI and API**), **Learn** (fold certified corrections back in). Ships a Next.js 16 frontend, FastAPI + LangChain backend, an ingestion worker, **Postgres + pgvector**, optional HashiCorp Vault, and Helm or Docker Compose deployment; NL-to-SQL is powered by **NVIDIA NIM**. **Why it's trending:** text-to-SQL agents have a correctness problem that no amount of retrieval fixes, and this is a major vendor shipping the governance layer as open source rather than a product. **What to know:** the README says the project is **currently not accepting external contributions** — open license, closed development. **[FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c)** — *"A 2.78-trillion-parameter model. One CPU. 8 GB of RAM."* Apache-2.0, **C99**, **10,451 stars** (reported **+351 today**), 1,644 forks, 26 open issues; the engine is **176 KB** of code with **no BLAS, no framework, no GPU**. The measured table is the pitch: **8 GB RAM → 26.5 s/token**, 32 GB → 24.2 s, 64 GB → 19.8 s, **128 GB+ → 5.6 s**, against a **1.56 TB** checkpoint on disk. Below 128 GB the whole model streams off NVMe on every step; at 128 GB+ it fits in memory and the disk wait disappears. **Output is byte-identical across all four configurations — only the clock changes.** v1.0.0 reportedly cut per-token math ~**8×**, chat follow-ups **3.9×** faster, long prompts about half as costly. macOS, Windows and NEON ports, chat mode, the `ultra` preset and faster MXFP4 kernels came from outside contributors. **Why it's trending:** Moonshot's K3.1 Pro weights landing today (above) turns this from a stunt into a usable path — the same 1.56 TB download, and anyone with a laptop and patience can run it. **What to know:** 26.5 seconds per token is a demonstration of *reachability*, not a workable interactive setup, and last push was **October 2**, so the stars are riding the weights news rather than active development. **[zhayujie/CowAgent](https://github.com/zhayujie/CowAgent)** — *an open-source personal AI assistant and agent harness that plans tasks, runs tools and skills, and self-evolves with memory and knowledge.* MIT, Python, **47,793 stars**, **10,415 forks**, 40 open issues, created **August 2022** — one of the longest-running projects on any of these boards, now pushed into the agent-harness category. Multi-agent, multi-model, multi-channel: plug in any major LLM provider and run it 24/7 on a personal machine or server, across the web and the major IM platforms; it controls your computer and external services, creates and runs **Skills**, and builds a personal knowledge base and long-term memory. **[finic-ai/kairos](https://github.com/finic-ai/kairos)** — *open-source real-time fraud and risk decisioning, pitched as an alternative to Sardine, Sift, Riskified and SEON.* Apache-2.0, TypeScript, **213 stars**, 10 forks — tiny, but **created October 30** and already a **104-point, 31-comment Show HN**. One call on every sign-up, login, order, payment and payout returns **approve, step up, review or block** with a risk score and reasons, drawn from the subject's history, the devices/cards/addresses it shares with others, and the session; every decision is kept with the signals behind it. Workflows can ask a decision model, score, branch, call webhooks, open cases and re-decide later; human review queues turn resolutions into labels. The two differentiators it claims over the commercial incumbents: **your coding agent tunes it** (there is an **MCP server** for Claude Code and Cursor, and the README's lead image is an agent running experiments on a workflow and picking the winning variant), and **decision models catch fraud before you have labels to train on**. Ships as `@finic-ai/kairos` on npm and `finic-kairos` on PyPI, with a hosted Kairos Cloud. **Why it's here on velocity rather than volume:** this is the clearest instance yet of the pattern worth watching — a regulated, label-starved production system shipped specifically so an agent can be the one tuning it. **What to know:** six days old, 213 stars, a commercial cloud attached; no production track record, and fraud decisioning is not a domain to adopt on a Show HN.
